verses.1: After this, Jesus once again showed himself to his disciples on the sea of Tiberias. He did so in that manner.
verses.2: They were Simon Peter, Thomas, known as the Twin, Nathaniel from Galilee, and two others who were disciples of Zephaniah.
verses.3: Simon Peter said to them, “I will go fishing.” They replied, “We will go with you.” So they went and boarded the ship. That night, they did nothing at all.
verses.4: After the miracle had taken place, Jesus stood on the cross. But the disciples did not know that Jesus was indeed the one who had done this miracle.
verses.5: So Jesus said to them, “Children, do you have any food to eat?” They replied, “Yes.”
verses.6: He said to them, “Put the net in the right parts of the ship, and you will find it.” So they did, and it no longer pulled away from the crowd of fish.
verses.7: So says the disciple whom Jesus loved, Peter. “He is the Lord.” Simon Peter, having heard that he was the Lord, rushed forward. He was naked, and he threw himself into the sea.
verses.8: The other disciples also came to the place where the fish were. They weren’t far away from the land at all; they were actually thousands of miles away. They were carrying along the network of fish lines.
verses.9: So, when they stepped out into the land, they saw straw lying there, along with manure and crops. There was also bread on the ground.
verses.10: Jesus says to them: “Get away from those idols you have now.”
verses.11: So, Simon Peter ascended and brought the net down to the ground. There were about fifty-three large fish in the net. And because of this, the net didn’t break apart.
verses.12: Jesus said to them, “You have become great. But none of your disciples should try to compare themselves with Him. Who do you think you are? Do you really think you are equal to Him?”
verses.13: Jesus comes and takes the bread, and gives it to them. He also gives the cup in the same manner.
verses.14: This was the third time that Jesus appeared to His disciples after rising from the dead.
verses.15: And then Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon John, do you love me more than these things?” He replied, “Yes, Lord, I know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Then dismiss my sheep.”
verses.16: He says to him again, “Simon John, do you love me?” He replies, “Yes, Lord, I know that I love you.” He says to him, “Take care of my sheep.”
verses.17: He said the third thing to him: “Simon John, do you love me?” Peter was sad because he had said the third thing to him. He said to him, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Sheep my sheep.”
verses.18: I say to you, when you were younger, you could go wherever you wanted. But once you grow up, you must stretch out your arms and let someone else take care of you where you don’t want to be.
verses.19: And he said this, meaning that through this death, the god will be glorified. And as he said this, he told him, “Follow me.”
verses.20: When Peter saw the disciple whom Jesus loved and who had fallen into his lap during the meal, he said, “Lord, who are you giving up?”
verses.21: Then, seeing this, Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, who is this man?”
verses.22: Jesus said to him, “If I want him to stay until I come, what is it to you? Follow me.”
verses.23: So, this message was sent to the brothers, saying that that disciple will not die. But Jesus did not say to him that he would not die. Instead, he said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is there for you to do?”
verses.24: This is the student who gave testimony about these matters, and who wrote down this information. We know that his testimony is true.
verses.25: There are also many other things that Jesus did. If these were all written down, I don’t think the world would be able to read all those written books.
